defect_observations.observation: Source extent: the worked order-of-magnitude estimate is Mahajan's lane-capacity calculation from Sec. 1.2 (printed pp. 6-7, correctly attributed at 073 lines 447-449). That section lies outside the unit's declared Chapter 1 extent, 'sections 1.3-1.5 only for the finite estimate example'. The in-extent 1.3-1.5 estimates (bill-volume tree, oil imports, multiple estimates; host lines 566-615) are handled as point estimates. The 1.3 train tree gets an input-range model (host lines 577-583) but no exhibited omitted-variable failure. The C04 success condition does not name a source example, so this was not scored as a gap.

Precision presentation: the 1.4 oil estimate is restated as 'about 3.33e9 barrels per year' from one-significant-figure inputs (20000, 30, 60, 2, 1/2), which the source itself rounds to 3e9, and is set beside the reported 3.34e9. The inputs are also listed without their units (miles per car-year, miles per gallon, gallons per barrel). This is not the C04 worked estimate, so it was not scored against C04.

Precision presentation: C' about 0.022 with chord 10 m and span 60 m gives C = 0.5 x 0.022 x 10/60, about 1/545, not 1/600 (the source rounds to about 1/600, printed p. 133). The range is then reported as 'about 9.8e6 m', two significant figures from one-significant-figure inputs; the source states about 1e7 m = 1e4 km, and the unrounded C would give about 9.3e6 m. This is an unearned-digit report outside the C04 worked estimate.

Precision and provenance: 'about 43.3 K' is three significant figures from F about 0.8 W/m^2. It uses the handbook's declared balance with a factor 1/4, not the source's box model F = sigma T^4 (printed p. 107, eq. 4.16), although the sentence opens 'Using the source's F ...'. Similarly, 'T sqrt(g/l) about 6.201' at line 326 comes from l about 0.65 m, where the source reports 'close to 6.20' (printed p. 149).

Correctness nuance (not scored): with n a dimensionless parameter, dimensions alone give q tau = G(z; n). Writing q tau/n = Phi(z) with Phi free of n uses the definitional premise q = n x car flow (lane-model definition, lines 96-98), which is not cited at this step.
